title: 20 EMA Pullback
teaches: The 20 EMA pullback as we trade it: a leader in a rising trend, above its 200-day with the 20 EMA over a rising 50-day, drifts quietly back to the rising 20 EMA, a session holds the line, the buy is a cent over that session's high at market in regular hours, the stop sits a few cents under its low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

facts.quote: we want the stock to fall back to a 20 day moving average after its ADX indicator has moved to a value above 30.
facts.claim: Raschke: the Holy Grail buys the fall back to the 20-day average after a strong trend.

facts.quote: 2. Look for a retracement in price to the 20 period exponential moving average. This will usually be accompanied by a turndown in the ADX.
facts.claim: Raschke's rule: look for a retracement to the 20-period exponential moving average.

facts.quote: 3. When the price touches the 20 period moving average, put a buy stop above the high of the previous bar.
facts.claim: Raschke's buy: a buy stop above the high of the previous bar once price touches the 20-period average.

facts.quote: 4. Once filled, enter a protective sell stop at the newly formed swing low. Trail stops as profits grow.
facts.claim: Raschke's stop: the newly formed swing low, trailed as profits grow.

facts.quote: This is a case where there is no reason to be in this trade.

facts.quote: On the 30-minute time frame, the ADX rose above 30, so we'll buy the first retracement to the 20-period EMA and look to exit on a push to new highs.
facts.claim: Raschke buys the first retracement to the 20-period EMA after a strong trend.

facts.quote: I use market orders most of the time.
facts.claim: Raschke uses market orders most of the time.

facts.quote: By focusing on the 10 and 20-day exponential moving averages (EMAs), you can identify key moments to buy stocks when the price dips into these levels after a strong rally.
facts.claim: Kell: buy the dip into the 10 and 20-day EMAs after a strong rally.

facts.quote: But always wait for confirmation that buyers are stepping in before making your trade.
facts.claim: Kell: always wait for confirmation that buyers are stepping in.

facts.quote: The EMA Crossback refers to the first time the stock price retests its moving averages after a strong upward move, called a “Wedge Pop.”
facts.claim: Kell: the EMA Crossback is the first retest of the averages after a Wedge Pop.

facts.quote: The EMA Crossback works best when the price gently moves sideways, allowing the moving averages to rise to the price.
facts.claim: Kell: the pullback works best when price drifts sideways and the rising averages catch up.

facts.quote: During the consolidation the stock price “surfs” the rising 10- and 20-day. and sometimes toe 50-day moving average.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: a leader surfs its rising 10 and 20-day lines and sometimes toes the 50-day.

facts.quote: Stop is always lows of the day and stop should not be wider than the ATR or ADR of the stock
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the stop is the low of the day, no wider than the stock's ATR or ADR.

facts.quote: A big move higher sometime in the past 1-3 months. This move can be anywhere from 30-100%+ and usually lasts a few days to a few weeks.
facts.claim: Kullamagi wants a big move of 30% to 100% or more in the past 1 to 3 months first.

facts.quote: If a beginner stick to the 10-day. You wait for the first CLOSE below the 10- day.
facts.claim: Kullamagi trails the 10-day and sells on the first close below it.

facts.quote: As long as the price remains above the 21-day EMA, any short-term movements can be considered noise, rather than a clear signal of a change in trend.
facts.claim: Keller: above the 21-day EMA, short-term moves are noise, not a change of trend.

facts.quote: The price is above the 21-day EMA, the 21-day is above the 50-day SMA, and the 50-day is above the 200-day SMA.
facts.claim: Keller's proper order: price over the 21-day EMA, over the 50-day, over the 200-day.

facts.quote: I think of the 21-day EMA as the first line of defense, an initial stop within an uptrend phase.
facts.claim: Keller calls the 21-day EMA the first line of defense in an uptrend.

facts.quote: chasing stocks hitting a new high in price can be the surest way to frustration
facts.claim: McGonagle: chasing new highs is the surest way to frustration; wait for the pullback.

facts.quote: While you can use either the shorter-term 10-day or the longer-term 21-day moving average, you’ll want to check the stock’s chart to uncover which one is the better indicator.

facts.quote: a moving average gives you a reason to study price action closely as it approaches, not a reason to act automatically.
facts.claim: Shannon: a moving average is a reason to watch price closely, not a reason to act automatically.

facts.claim: Shannon's trade ideas use stops 2 to 3% from the entry.

facts.claim: AlphaTrends: buying strength after a controlled pullback is not chasing an extended rally.

facts.quote: Place your stop-loss just below the most recent swing low or consolidation base.

facts.claim: A3: stop first, a few cents under the day's low; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up, never wider; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.quote: Shares = account × risk % ÷ (entry − stop), rounded down, then capped: the size is the SMALLER of the risk-based size and the position cap

facts.quote: "I almost never take a loss greater than 3%": the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy (a loss on the position, not the account).
facts.claim: A13: the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy.

facts.quote: A gap against the stop: the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. The low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.
facts.claim: B20: on a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

facts.claim: B20's ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.

facts.claim: B22: no new buys in the 3 days before a report; hold through one only if up 5R.

facts.claim: C28: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

facts.claim: C29: skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day average.

walkthroughs.title: GE, January 2024: the low kisses the line
steps: GE, January 2024. A leader in a rising trend drifts four days back to its rising 20 EMA on 0.78x volume.
The hold session: the low kisses the line to the cent and closes above it. Above the 50-day and 200-day.
Next session trades a cent over the hold candle's high. Buy at market, 100.39. Stop a few cents under its low, 99.07.
Failure mode: a slice back through the line that takes the day's low. Instead, 3R in 5 sessions. A third comes off.

walkthroughs.title: NVDA, May 2023: the textbook leader, out before the report
steps: NVDA, May 2023. A rising line, a light-volume four-day rest, 1.4 ATR off the high, pullback volume 0.74x.
The hold session closes above the line. Buy a cent over its high at market, 28.79. Stop under its low, 28.02.
3R in 3 sessions: a third off, stop to breakeven. It stood at 3.9R the day before the report.
Hold through a report only if up 5R. We are out before the gap. The rule costs one gap and saves many.

walkthroughs.title: CRM, June 2020: the shallow shakeout
steps: CRM, June 2020. A four-day pullback, 2.4 ATR off the high on 0.76x volume. The low dips 0.28 ATR under the line.
The same session closes back above the 20 EMA. That is a shakeout, not a lost line. The hold is in.
Next session trades a cent over the hold candle's high. Buy at market, 183.72. Stop a few cents under its low, 179.97.
Failure mode: a second close under the line before the trigger. Instead, 3R in 2 sessions. A third off, stop to breakeven.

questions.q: In one line, what is a 20 EMA pullback?
choices: A leader resting on its rising 20 EMA
A line lost for weeks and then retaken
A box under a flat ceiling
A V-bottom off the 200-day
questions.answer: A leader resting on its rising 20 EMA
questions.why: A leader resting back onto its rising 20 EMA. Kullamagi: the stock surfs the rising 10 and 20-day. Raschke: a retracement to the 20-period EMA.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback is a leader catching its breath at a line that is still rising.

wrong.A line lost for weeks and then retaken: That is a Remount. A pullback holds its line; it does not lose it for weeks.
wrong.A box under a flat ceiling: That is a flat base. A pullback is a dip to a moving line, not a rest under a level.
wrong.A V-bottom off the 200-day: A pullback sits in a rising trend above the 200-day. A V-bottom is a reversal.

questions.q: Which line must the hold session close above, by our hard rule?
choices: The 200-day simple average
The 50-day SMA, if it is rising
The 9 EMA, closing back over it
No line; the touch is enough
questions.why: The 200-day simple moving average. No longs below it. AlphaTrends: above the 200-day the larger trend is innocent until proven guilty.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day there is no pullback to buy, only a bounce.

wrong.The 50-day SMA, if it is rising: The 50-day is part of the context, not the hard line. The hard line is the 200-day.
wrong.The 9 EMA, closing back over it: The 9 EMA is a confirming sign in grading, not a gate.
wrong.No line; the touch is enough: The touch is the pattern. The 200-day is the context that must be there first.

questions.q: On a 20 EMA pullback the stop goes a few cents under the low of the session that held the line.
questions.why: True. A few cents under the hold session's low, not exactly on it. Kullamagi: the stop is always the low of the day.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the hold session's low.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The 20 EMA must be ___: higher than it was 10 sessions earlier.
questions.why: Rising. Higher than 10 sessions earlier. Kell: the averages rise to the price; Kullamagi: the stock surfs the rising lines.
questions.lesson_line: A rising line is the whole setup. A flat one is a different chart.

questions.q: A session held the 20 EMA and closed above it. Where is the buy we draw on the chart?
choices: A cent over the hold candle's high
At the close of the hold session
A limit order resting on the 20 EMA
A close back over the 9 EMA
questions.answer: A cent over the hold candle's high
questions.why: A cent over the hold candle's high, at market, on a later session. Raschke: a buy stop above the high of the previous bar once price touches the line.
questions.lesson_line: The hold candle sets the trigger. Over its high, we are in.

wrong.At the close of the hold session: The close is where a scanner marks the day. Our buy is the trade over the hold candle's high.
wrong.A limit order resting on the 20 EMA: That buys before anything has held. Never buy before a session holds the line.
wrong.A close back over the 9 EMA: The 9 EMA remount is a confirming sign in grading, not the trigger.

questions.q: Entries on a 20 EMA pullback are limit orders placed on the 20 EMA, in regular hours only.
questions.why: False. Entries are market orders, placed in regular hours only. Raschke: I use market orders most of the time.
questions.lesson_line: Market order the moment it trades. Regular hours only.

questions.q: If the trend is strong enough, you may buy the first touch of the 20 EMA before any session has held it.
questions.why: False. Never buy before a session actually holds the line. Kell: always wait for confirmation that buyers are stepping in.
questions.lesson_line: The line is a place to watch, not a reason to act. Let a session hold it first.

questions.q: During the pullback the session's low reaches under the 50-day SMA. Which card is it now, if anything?
choices: The 50-day MA pullback
Still the 20 EMA pullback
A Remount of the 50-day
A bull flag on the 50-day
questions.why: The 50-day form of the moving-average pullback, if anything. The 20 EMA pullback's low holds above the 50-day; once it reaches the 50-day, the 50-day is the line.
questions.lesson_line: Name the line the low touched. The 50-day is a different card.

wrong.Still the 20 EMA pullback: The 20 EMA pullback's low holds above the 50-day. This low went through it.
wrong.A Remount of the 50-day: A Remount is a line lost and retaken, not a dip. One session's low under the 50-day is not that.
wrong.A bull flag on the 50-day: A flag needs a pole. The question here is only which line the low touched.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The pullback lasts 2 to ___ sessions from the swing high to the hold session.
questions.why: 15. Two to 15 sessions from the swing high. The scan's examples ran four to ten days.
questions.lesson_line: Count the sessions: two to fifteen. Past three weeks it is not our pullback.

questions.q: Which pullback into the 20 EMA is orderly by our card?
choices: Small red days on quiet volume
One red day of 3 ATR into the line
A red day on 2x the 50-day volume
A gap down through the 50-day
questions.answer: Small red days on quiet volume
questions.why: Small red days on quiet volume. No down day larger than 2 ATR and none on more than 1.5 times the 50-day volume. Shannon wants volume contracting on pullbacks.
questions.lesson_line: Orderly means small bars and quiet volume. A big red day is selling, not resting.

wrong.One red day of 3 ATR into the line: A 3 ATR down day is past the 2 ATR line. Not orderly.
wrong.A red day on 2x the 50-day volume: Over 1.5 times the 50-day volume on a down day is distribution.
wrong.A gap down through the 50-day: That broke the 50-day. The 20 EMA pullback is off.

questions.q: A stock drifting along its 20 EMA, no swing high at least 1 ATR above the hold low, has not pulled back.
questions.why: True. The pullback is at least 1 ATR off the swing high. That is measured from the highest high of the last 11 sessions to the hold session's low. No dip, no pullback.
questions.lesson_line: You need something to pull back from. Measure the dip in ATR.

questions.q: Does Thursday's low count as a touch by the card?
choices: Yes; inside 1 ATR under the line
No; the low must stay above the line
No; it must close on the line
questions.answer: Yes; inside 1 ATR under the line
questions.why: Yes. The low may sit anywhere from 0.25 ATR above to 1 ATR below the 20 EMA. 48.30 is under 50.00 by less than one ATR of 2.00, and the session closed back above the line.
questions.lesson_line: A touch has a band: a little above the line, up to one ATR under it.

wrong.No; the low must stay above the line: A low up to 1 ATR under the line still counts. The line gets run through; it is not a wall.
wrong.No; it must close on the line: The close has to be at or above the line, not on it. 50.60 is above.

questions.story: The 20 EMA is 50.00 and ATR is 2.00. Thursday's low is 48.30 and it closes at 50.60, above the line.

questions.q: Two closes in a row under the 20 EMA during the pullback end the setup until it sets up again.
questions.why: True. A close more than 0.5 ATR under the 20 EMA ends the setup. So do two closes in a row under it. There is no trade until it sets up again.
questions.lesson_line: One shakeout is allowed. Two closes under the line is a line lost.

questions.q: A scanner puts the stop at the line minus 1 ATR. Why is that not our stop?
choices: Too wide; the day's low is the stop
Too tight; it sits inside the noise
It is fine for a fast mover
Because the 50-day is the stop
questions.answer: Too wide; the day's low is the stop
questions.why: Too wide. The line minus 1 ATR is wider than one ATR whenever the entry is above the line. Our stop is a few cents under the hold session's low.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is a price under a candle, not a line minus a cushion.

wrong.Too tight; it sits inside the noise: It is the other way round: a cushion under the line is wider than the day's low, not tighter.
wrong.It is fine for a fast mover: A fast mover gets the same rule: a few cents under the hold session's low.
wrong.Because the 50-day is the stop: The 50-day is not a stop either. The stop is the hold session's low.

questions.q: The stop can be a close under the 20 EMA that you watch for, as long as you act on it.
questions.why: False. Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head. A close under a line cannot sit with the broker as an order.
questions.lesson_line: A stop in your head is a debate. A stop with the broker is an appointment.

questions.q: On the hold session, where does the card want the 20 EMA against the 50-day SMA?
choices: Above a rising 50-day SMA
Below the 50-day, catching up
Crossing it that session
Anywhere, as long as it rises
questions.why: Above a 50-day that is itself higher than 10 sessions earlier. Keller's proper order: price over the 21-day, over the 50-day, over the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Stacked and rising: 20 over 50 over 200. Then look at the dip.

wrong.Below the 50-day, catching up: A 20 EMA under the 50-day is a stock in repair, not a leader resting.
wrong.Crossing it that session: A cross is the line changing sides. We want the order already settled.
wrong.Anywhere, as long as it rises: It is the context. A pullback in the wrong order is a bounce in a downtrend.

questions.q: Is this a 20 EMA pullback?
choices: No; a flattening line is off
Yes; the touch is what counts
Yes, at half size
questions.answer: No; a flattening line is off
questions.why: No. A 20 EMA that is not higher than 10 sessions earlier has flattened, and the setup is off before any trigger. NVDA's late tap in 2025 failed exactly this way.
questions.lesson_line: A tired line does not hold. Pass the tap of a flattening 20 EMA.

wrong.Yes; the touch is what counts: The touch is the pattern. The rising line is the context, and it is gone.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Size does not fix a flat line. The rule is no trade.

questions.story: A stock has run four months. Its 20 EMA now sits lower than it was 10 sessions ago, and price drifts into it again.

questions.q: Buy the hold?
choices: No; a report inside 3 sessions
Yes; a first tap is the best tap
Yes, half size
questions.why: No. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. If it is still a setup after the report, it can hold again.
questions.lesson_line: A hold two days before earnings is a coin flip with a story. Wait.

wrong.Yes; a first tap is the best tap: The tap is fine and the calendar says no. The earnings rule is a hard line.
wrong.Yes, half size: Size does not fix a report. Smaller is still in.

questions.story: A leader's first tap of its rising 20 EMA holds today and closes above the line. The company reports in two sessions.

questions.q: Bought the hold at 147.30 with the stop at 145.05. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 154.05. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. A third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: The last third of a 20 EMA pullback winner trails which line, by our default?
choices: The 10-day or the 21-day line
The 20 EMA, from the first day
The 50-day only, on a close
No trail; sell it all at 5R
questions.why: The 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one, sold on a close below it. Kullamagi: wait for the first close below the 10-day.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the rising average. Sell the close below it, not the touch.

wrong.The 20 EMA, from the first day: A named mistake: trailing under the 20 EMA from day one lets normal noise stop a trade bought at the line.
wrong.The 50-day only, on a close: Our default trails the 10-day or the 21-day, not the 50-day alone.
wrong.No trail; sell it all at 5R: 5R is the second third, not the exit. The last third rides the trail.

questions.q: We buy this pullback in leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.why: True. Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups. Bonde: pullbacks in small, tired names make bag holders.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback in a laggard is a dip in a downtrend. Buy the leaders.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A down day into the line on more than ___ times the 50-day average volume is distribution, not a pullback.
questions.why: 1.5. Heavy selling into the line is distribution, and the setup is off before any trigger. Shannon wants volume contracting on pullbacks.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet into the line is a rest. Loud into the line is selling.

questions.q: What happened to your trade?
choices: Stopped; a planned loss
Still in; it closed above the stop
Add; the close held the line
questions.why: Stopped. The stop is the exit, and the low traded through it. The close back at 59.21 does not undo that; GILD did exactly this and went on without us.
questions.lesson_line: A loss taken at the stop is the system working, not a mistake.

wrong.Still in; it closed above the stop: The stop order fired at the low. A close above it afterwards is a different trade.
wrong.Add; the close held the line: Full size at one price with one stop. No adding, and nothing to add to.

questions.story: You bought the hold at 60.50 with the stop at 59.17. Next day the low prints 58.57 and the stock closes back at 59.21.

questions.q: Ten trading days after the buy the trade sits at 0.6R, doing nothing. Our rule?
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
Hold; the stop will do the exiting
Add a third to average up
Move the stop to breakeven
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money. Raschke on a stalled pullback: no reason to be in this trade.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing. The money has somewhere better to be.

wrong.Hold; the stop will do the exiting: The stop is one exit. The time stop is the other, and ten days have passed.
wrong.Add a third to average up: No adding, and nothing is working. The rule frees the money.
wrong.Move the stop to breakeven: Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R. At 0.6R the time stop applies.

questions.q: The highest high of the last 11 sessions is 120.00, ATR is 3.00 and the hold session's low is 117.60. How deep is the pullback, in ATR?
questions.why: 0.8 ATR. The swing high minus the hold low, divided by ATR. The card wants at least 1 ATR; this is a drift along the line, not a pullback to it.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the dip in ATR. Under one, there was nothing to pull back from.

questions.q: Fill 100.39. The hold candle's low is 99.10 and the stop sits three cents under it. How far below the fill is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 1.31%. A few cents under the hold candle's low, well inside the 3% the stop usually sits within. That was GE's 1.3% stop.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Account 40,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 95.90, stop 93.85. How many shares?
questions.why: 97. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size, never the other way round.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. You never pick a size and back-fit a stop.

questions.q: Buy the open?
choices: No; over 4% past the trigger
Yes; the gap shows strength
Yes, buying half the usual size
questions.why: No. 52.40 is more than 4% over the 50.00 trigger. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the hold candle, so the distance grows and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the trigger and I am done. I would rather miss it than chase it.

wrong.Yes; the gap shows strength: Strength and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Yes, buying half the usual size: Half of a bad entry is still a bad entry. The rule is skip.

questions.story: The hold candle's high is 50.00. Next morning the stock gaps open at 52.40 and keeps going.

questions.q: What do you do at 10:40?
choices: Buy now; stop under Wednesday's low
Wait for Thursday's close to confirm
Place a limit order on the 20 EMA
questions.answer: Buy now; stop under Wednesday's low
questions.why: Buy at market as it trades a cent over the hold candle's high. The stop sits a few cents under the hold candle's low, or under today's low if that is lower. The trigger is the trade through, not the close.
questions.lesson_line: Alert at the hold candle's high. When it trades, you buy; you do not wait for the bell.

wrong.Wait for Thursday's close to confirm: Waiting for the close can cost a day's move. The trigger fired at 10:40.
wrong.Place a limit order on the 20 EMA: A limit on the line buys a second dip that may not come, and buys before any hold.

questions.story: Wednesday's low tagged the rising 20 EMA and the session closed above the line. Thursday opens flat and at 10:40 trades 61.26, a cent over Wednesday's high.

questions.q: Is this the 20 EMA pullback?
choices: No; the low reached the 50-day
Yes; the 20 EMA was tagged too
Yes; both lines held the close
questions.why: No. The hold session's low must hold above the 50-day. This low sat under 408.58, so it is the 50-day form of the moving-average pullback, if anything. HD did this and stopped.
questions.lesson_line: When the low reaches the 50-day, the 50-day is the line. Judge it on that card.

wrong.Yes; the 20 EMA was tagged too: The 20 EMA was on the way down. The low went through it to the 50-day.
wrong.Yes; both lines held the close: The close is not the test here. The low broke the 50-day, which ends the 20 EMA card.

questions.story: The pullback low prints 401.01. The 50-day SMA sits at 408.58 and the 20 EMA at 408.60.

questions.q: A 20 EMA pullback can be an add-on to a position you already hold, at the same stop.
questions.why: False. It is a new trade at full size, at one price with one stop; no adding, no pilot.
questions.lesson_line: One price, one stop, full size. The pullback is a trade, not a top-up.

questions.q: What is the stop now?
choices: 96.10, the first 30-minute low
Sell at the open, 96.50
No stop until it reclaims 98.10
questions.why: 96.10. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. That low is inside the 2R ceiling, so it is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Sell at the open, 96.50: The gap rule gives it the first 30 minutes. The open is not the decision.
wrong.No stop until it reclaims 98.10: There is always a stop. The new one is the 30-minute low.

questions.story: You bought the hold at 100.20 with the stop at 98.10. It opens at 96.50 on a sector headline. The first 30-minute bar's low is 96.10.

questions.q: Where does the stop go now?
choices: To breakeven, the entry
It stays under the hold candle
A close under the 20 EMA
questions.why: To breakeven. The stop moves to the entry between 2R and 5R, and the first trim is the natural moment.
questions.lesson_line: Take the third, move the stop to the entry. The trade is now free.

wrong.It stays under the hold candle: The stop only moves up. At 3R it moves to the entry.
wrong.A close under the 20 EMA: A close under a line cannot sit as an order, and trailing the line this early is a named mistake.

questions.story: Your 20 EMA pullback buy reaches 3R on day three and you sell a third.

questions.q: The market reading is Yellow. What does that do to this setup?
choices: Smaller and fewer
Full risk, as in Green
Only A+ setups
No longs at all
questions.why: Smaller and fewer. Green is full risk; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange only A+; Red mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market before the line. Yellow trims the size and the count.

wrong.Full risk, as in Green: That is Green. Yellow cuts size and the number of positions.
wrong.Only A+ setups: That is Orange. Yellow still allows A and B setups, smaller.
wrong.No longs at all: That is closer to Red. Yellow still trades, smaller and fewer.

questions.q: Can you buy it?
choices: Yes; a new trade on the new hold
No; one try per pullback
No; wait a week after a stop-out
questions.answer: Yes; a new trade on the new hold
questions.why: Yes. After a failed hold the way back in is a new hold session. It brings its own trigger and stop, as a new trade. At most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a verdict on the setup. The next hold is a new trade.

wrong.No; one try per pullback: The limit is 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, not one.
wrong.No; wait a week after a stop-out: There is no waiting period. There is a new trigger, and this is one.

questions.story: Your hold buy stopped out on Tuesday. On Thursday the stock sits on its rising 20 EMA again and a new session holds it.

questions.q: After a third comes off at 3R, the rest of the position is sold at 5R.
questions.why: False. After the first third at 3R: another third at 5R, then trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, trail the rest.

questions.q: Which pullback grades higher?
choices: The quiet drift
The heavy one; buyers will show
Equal; the touch is the touch
questions.why: The quiet drift. Our A+ cue is a quiet pullback, lower volume each day, small bars. Heavy selling into the line is the B- cue. TraderLion: a slow drift into the EMAs is ideal.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet into the line grades up. Loud into the line grades down.

wrong.The heavy one; buyers will show: Heavy red days into the line are sellers showing, not buyers. That is the B- cue.
wrong.Equal; the touch is the touch: The touch is the pattern. How price got there is the grade.

questions.story: Two six-day pullbacks to the 20 EMA. One drifts down on 0.7x volume with small bars. The other has two heavy red days into the line.

questions.q: What is it?
choices: A lost line; not a pullback
A 20 EMA pullback with a shakeout
A Remount of the 50-day line
questions.answer: A lost line; not a pullback
questions.why: A lost line. Three closes under the 20 EMA is past the one shakeout the card allows. There is no trade until it sets up again. AAPL showed this in January 2022, the deepest close 0.73 ATR under the line.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the line. One is a shakeout; three is a line lost.

wrong.A 20 EMA pullback with a shakeout: A pullback allows at most one close under the line, reclaimed the next session. This had three.
wrong.A Remount of the 50-day line: Too few closes under. A Remount is a 50-day or 200-day lost for five or more closes.

questions.story: Over a five-session pullback the stock closes under its 20 EMA on three days, the deepest 0.73 ATR under. Then it closes back above the line.

questions.q: Take the pullback?
choices: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
Yes; a clean pattern is the pattern
Yes, at half the normal size
questions.answer: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
questions.why: No. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. Bonde: buying such pullbacks on most small caps would make you a bag holder.
questions.lesson_line: A clean tap on a thin stock is still a thin stock.

wrong.Yes; a clean pattern is the pattern: The pattern is fine and the stock is not ours. The liquidity rule comes before the chart.
wrong.Yes, at half the normal size: Size does not make a thin stock liquid.

questions.story: A tidy four-day drift to the 20 EMA on a $7 stock that trades about $5 million a day.

questions.q: What do you do, and what was the tell?
choices: Stopped out; a late tap of a tired line
Hold; it will remount the line
Widen the stop to the 50-day
questions.answer: Stopped out; a late tap of a tired line
questions.why: Stopped out, by the order. The tell was the 20 EMA already flattening after a four-month run; a flattening line is off before the trigger. NVDA then sat under its 20 EMA for weeks.
questions.lesson_line: Late in a run the line flattens and the taps stop holding. Pass them.

wrong.Hold; it will remount the line: The stop is the exit. Hoping for a remount is how a small loss becomes a big one.
wrong.Widen the stop to the 50-day: The stop only moves up, never wider.

questions.story: Late in a four-month run you bought a tap of the 20 EMA at 181.91, stop 178.01. Next day the low hits 175.49 and the stock closes under the line.

questions.q: A long 8% above its 10-day average is too stretched to buy, even at a pullback trigger.
questions.why: False. The skip line is a long more than 10% above its 10-day average. At 8% it passes this test.
questions.lesson_line: A stretched buy is a chase with a different name.

questions.q: Bought at 28.79, stop 28.02. The stock trades to 32.64. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. The gain divided by the fill minus the stop. That is where the second third comes off.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 5R is the second trim.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Sell a big part into it
Hold everything; the trend is up
Add; strength is strength
questions.answer: Sell a big part into it
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. A climax run on your own long, gaps and the heaviest volume of the run, is where we sell into strength. A judgment call, and the rule says lean to selling.
questions.lesson_line: When your winner goes vertical, sell them what they want.

wrong.Hold everything; the trend is up: A vertical burst is the end of a leg more often than the middle. Bank some.
wrong.Add; strength is strength: No adding, and never into a climax. That is the top of the risk, not the bottom.

questions.story: Your pullback buy is up 9R in two weeks. Today it gaps up again, the third straight up day, on the heaviest volume of the run.

questions.q: If the stock opens above a trim level, that trim is taken at the open.
questions.why: True. If a stock opens above a trim level, 3R or 5R, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through a trim level is the trim. Take it at the open.

questions.q: Which low does the stop go under?
choices: 93.60, the lower of the two
93.88, the hold candle's low
The 20 EMA itself
questions.why: 93.60. The stop goes a few cents under the lower of the holding candle's low and the trigger session's low. The trigger day went lower, so it sets the stop.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits under the lowest low of the hold and the trigger day.

wrong.93.88, the hold candle's low: The trigger day printed a lower low first. A stop at 93.88 would sit above a low the stock has already made.
wrong.The 20 EMA itself: A line is not a stop order. The stop is a price under a candle's low.

questions.story: The holding candle's low is 93.88. The next session dips to 93.60 first, then trades over the hold candle's high and you buy.

questions.q: Price holds the 20 EMA and the same session closes back over the 9 EMA. On our card, that 9 EMA remount is what?
choices: A confirming sign, not a gate
The trigger for the buy order
An invalidation of the hold
The line the stop is placed at
questions.answer: A confirming sign, not a gate
questions.why: A confirming sign in grading, not a gate. A close back over the 9 EMA says buyers showed, and grades the hold up. It is not the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: The 9 EMA remount is a plus on the grade, not the buy.

wrong.The trigger for the buy order: Some playbooks make it the buy. Our card makes it a confirming sign.
wrong.An invalidation of the hold: A close back over a faster line is strength, not a failure.
wrong.The line the stop is placed at: The stop is a few cents under the hold session's low, never a line.

questions.q: Growing sales and earnings come first in grading a pullback buy; the chart is the tie-breaker.
questions.why: False. Prefer stocks with growing sales and earnings, but the chart comes first.
questions.lesson_line: Numbers help. The chart decides.

questions.q: Which name fits?
choices: EMA Crossback; the first test
20 EMA pullback; a tap is a tap
Remount; the 20 EMA was retaken
questions.why: The EMA Crossback. Count the sessions since the stock closed back above both the 9 and 20 EMA out of a decline. The first test soon after that pop is Kell's crossback. A 20 EMA pullback taps a line that has been rising for weeks after an advance off it.
questions.lesson_line: Just reclaimed and tested for the first time is a crossback. Long rising and tapped again is a pullback.

wrong.20 EMA pullback; a tap is a tap: A pullback taps a line that has been rising for weeks after an advance off it. This line was reclaimed eight sessions ago.
wrong.Remount; the 20 EMA was retaken: The 20 EMA was retaken eight sessions ago and has held since. The test now is a pullback to it, not a retake.

questions.story: The stock spent weeks under its averages, then closed back over the 9 and 20 EMA eight sessions ago. Now it tests those averages for the first time.

questions.q: Which name fits?
choices: A Remount; a lost line retaken
A 20 EMA pullback, then a bounce
An undercut and rally of a line
questions.answer: A Remount; a lost line retaken
questions.why: A Remount. Nine closes in a row under the 50-day is a line lost, and today's close back above it is the retake. A pullback allows at most one close under its line.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the line. A week or more under it and back is a Remount, not a pullback.

wrong.A 20 EMA pullback, then a bounce: A pullback allows at most one close under the 20 EMA. This stock lost its 50-day for nine sessions.
wrong.An undercut and rally of a line: An undercut and rally reclaims its level within a few sessions. Nine closes under is a lost line.

questions.story: The stock closed under its 50-day for nine sessions in a row, then today closed back above it on big volume.

questions.q: Which name fits, and what decides it?
choices: Bull flag; the pole decides
20 EMA pullback; the line decides
EMA Crossback; the pop decides
questions.why: A bull flag. Measure the pole: a gain of 20% or more inside 20 sessions. A tight drift of a few days after it is the flag. A 20 EMA pullback needs no pole, only a rising line.
questions.lesson_line: A pole in front of the drift makes it a flag. No pole, just a rising line, makes it a pullback.

wrong.20 EMA pullback; the line decides: The drift did reach the 20 EMA, but a 24% pole in 12 sessions names the flag first.
wrong.EMA Crossback; the pop decides: A crossback follows a reclaim of the averages out of a decline. This stock rose in a trend and paused.

questions.story: The stock rose 24% in 12 sessions, then drifted five days back onto its 20 EMA on quiet volume.

questions.q: Which name fits?
choices: The MAU&R costume of the U&R
The 20 EMA pullback
A Remount
questions.answer: The MAU&R costume of the U&R
questions.why: The undercut and rally in its moving-average costume. Ask what the buy is. By our current default, a low that undercut the 20 EMA, bought as the move back above the line, is the U&R.
questions.lesson_line: Same line, different buy. Buying the move back through the line is the U&R, not the pullback.

wrong.The 20 EMA pullback: Its buy is the turn off a held line, such as red to green. Buying the move back above the line is the U&R.
wrong.A Remount: The line was under water for two hours, not a week or more. That is an undercut, not a lost line.

questions.story: At 10 am the low breaks 1% under the 20 EMA. By noon price is back above the line and you buy the move back through it.

questions.q: Are these 20 EMA pullbacks?
choices: No; not longs under the 200-day
Yes; the 20 EMA held both times
Yes, but at half the usual size
questions.why: No. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average unless it is a parabolic long. A bounce into the 20 EMA under a falling 200-day is a bear-market bounce, not a pullback in a trend.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day a hold of the 20 EMA is a bounce. We do not buy bounces.

wrong.Yes; the 20 EMA held both times: The holds are real and the context is wrong. The 200-day rule is a hard line.
wrong.Yes, but at half the usual size: Size does not fix the context. Under the 200-day there is no long.

questions.story: In a bear market a stock bounces off its 20 EMA twice in a month. Both times price is under a falling 200-day.

questions.q: The card wants the 200-day no lower than it was 20 sessions earlier; a 200-day still falling fails the context.
questions.why: True. The card's context line: the 200-day SMA is not lower than it was 20 sessions earlier.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day, and the 200-day not falling. Both halves matter.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: No; distribution into the line
Yes; the hold is clean
Yes; volume on a red day is good
questions.why: No. A down day into the line on more than 1.5 times the 50-day volume is distribution, not a pullback. The setup is off. INTC did this in 2017 and stopped.
questions.lesson_line: One loud red day into the line is the sellers' tell. The hold does not erase it.

wrong.Yes; the hold is clean: The hold session was fine. The pullback behind it was not.
wrong.Yes; volume on a red day is good: Volume on a red day is sellers. We want quiet into the line and loud out of it.

questions.story: A five-day pullback to the 20 EMA holds and closes above the line. One of its down days ran on 2.3x the 50-day volume.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The same stock: at most ___ tries in a week and 6 in a month.
questions.why: 3. At most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month on one stock. Each is a new trade on a new hold.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week. After that the stock is telling you something.

questions.q: Was the loss a mistake?
choices: No; the rules were followed
Yes; re-buy at 546 and hold
Yes; the stop needed more room
questions.why: No. The stop is the exit and it did its job on a one-day shakeout. A re-buy at the old price is not a rule; a new hold session with its own trigger is. CAT ran to 610 without us, and that is the cost of being there for the ones that work.
questions.lesson_line: A loss taken at plan is the system working, even when the stock runs after.

wrong.Yes; re-buy at 546 and hold: After a stop-out you buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade. A chase back in is not a trigger.
wrong.Yes; the stop needed more room: The stop was already 3.1% wide. The stop only moves up, never wider.

questions.story: You bought a hold at 558.32 with the stop at 540.97, about 3.1% wide. Next day the stock gaps to 543.35, the low prints 538.05 and the stop fires. It closes 546.88 and reaches 610 within a month.

questions.q: Hold through the report?
choices: No; hold through only if up 5R
Yes; it is nearly at the 5R line
Yes, after selling half first
questions.answer: No; hold through only if up 5R
questions.why: No. We hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R, and 3.9R is not 5R. NVDA's May 2023 hold sat at 3.9R the day before its report; the rule had us out before the gap.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings is a gap you cannot stop. Five R buys the ticket; almost does not.

wrong.Yes; it is nearly at the 5R line: Almost is under the line. The rule is 5R, not nearly 5R.
wrong.Yes, after selling half first: Half of a 3.9R cushion is still under the 5R line.

questions.story: Your 20 EMA pullback buy is up 3.9R the day before the company reports.

questions.q: The trigger is 45.00 and the stock opens at 46.62, above it. How far above the trigger is the open, in percent?
questions.why: 3.6%. The open over the trigger, minus one. Inside the 4% line, so the fill at the open is allowed; the stop still sits under the hold candle, so the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the gap against the trigger. Inside 4% you may take the open.

questions.q: What happens to the last third?
choices: Sold on the close under it
Held; the stop is at breakeven
Added to, buying the dip
questions.answer: Sold on the close under it
questions.why: Sold. Two thirds are banked. The last third trails the 10-day for a fast mover or the 21-day for a steadier one. A close below the line is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: Two thirds banked, the last third on the trail. The close below the line is the exit.

wrong.Held; the stop is at breakeven: Breakeven is the floor, not the plan. The trail is the exit for the last third.
wrong.Added to, buying the dip: Full size at one price; no adding. A close under the trail is an exit, not an add.

questions.story: You bought ILMN's hold at 95.90, stop 93.85. 3R came in 10 sessions and a third came off; 5R and another third. Weeks later the stock closes under its 21-day.

questions.q: A 20 EMA that crosses under the 50-day SMA before the trigger ends the pullback setup.
questions.why: True. A 20 EMA that flattens, turns down or crosses under the 50-day ends the setup before entry. Keller's proper order has the 21-day over the 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: The fast line under the slow line is not a pullback. It is a trend in trouble.

questions.q: How many mistakes, and which?
choices: Two: no real stop, and the size
None; the line is a fine stop
One: the size, if the trade works
questions.answer: Two: no real stop, and the size
questions.why: Two. A close under the line cannot sit with the broker as an order. Sizing for a 1.5% stop when the exit is 4% away risks far more than the plan. Stop first, then the size from it.
questions.lesson_line: A line is not an order, and a size is never chosen before the stop.

wrong.None; the line is a fine stop: A line is a place to watch. The stop is a price with the broker, a few cents under the hold session's low.
wrong.One: the size, if the trade works: Whether the trade works does not change the rule. Both the stop and the size were wrong before the open.

questions.story: A member sets the stop as a close under the 20 EMA, about 4% away. The member sizes the position as if the stop were 1.5% away.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
choices: Market 100.39; stop 99.07; third at 3R
Limit on the 20 EMA; stop 95.00; hold
Market at the close; stop 50-day; 2R
questions.why: Market at 100.39 as it trades a cent over the hold candle's high. The stop is 99.07, a few cents under the low. A third comes off at 3R. GE reached 3R in 5 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open; execute it without a debate.

wrong.Limit on the 20 EMA; stop 95.00; hold: A limit on the line buys before a hold, and a stop at 95.00 is nowhere near the hold candle's low.
wrong.Market at the close; stop 50-day; 2R: The trigger is the trade over the hold candle's high, not the close, and the 50-day is not a stop.

questions.story: GE, January 2024. Four days drift to the rising 20 EMA on 0.78x volume. The low kisses the line to the cent and the session closes above it. Its low is 99.10 and its high is 100.38.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: Pass; Orange buys A+ only
Buy it; a hold is a hold
Buy at half size
questions.why: Pass. Orange allows only A+ setups, and this one grades B. The market reading sits above the setup; the hold cannot see the market.
questions.lesson_line: In Orange a B setup stays on the bench, however clean the hold.

wrong.Buy it; a hold is a hold: The hold is real. Orange narrows you to A+ and this is a B.
wrong.Buy at half size: Orange is about grade, not size. A B setup does not trade at all.

questions.story: The market reading is Orange. A leader holds its rising 20 EMA on quiet volume, the second tap of this run; you grade it B.

questions.q: Take the trigger?
choices: Yes; a shallow shakeout that held
No; any dip under the line is off
No; wait for a second hold
questions.answer: Yes; a shallow shakeout that held
questions.why: Yes. The low dipped a little under the line and the same session closed back above it: a shakeout, not a lost line. CRM did this in June 2020 and reached 3R in 2 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: A low under the line that closes back above it is a shakeout. The hold stands.

wrong.No; any dip under the line is off: The low may sit up to 1 ATR under the line. What ends the setup is a close well under it, or two closes under.
wrong.No; wait for a second hold: There is nothing to wait for. The session held and the next one triggered.

questions.story: The hold session's low dips 0.28 ATR under the 20 EMA and it closes back above the line the same day. Next session it trades over that candle's high.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the hold session. Judge the touch, the 50-day and the slope of the line. Take it or pass.
choices: Take it; the low kissed the line
Pass; the low reached the 50-day
Pass; the line is falling
questions.answer: Take it; the low kissed the line
questions.why: Take it. The low kissed the rising 20 EMA to the cent and the session closed above it, with the 50-day well below. A four-day drift on 0.78x volume. It broke out the next day and reached 3R in 5 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: The low on the line, the close above it, the 50-day below: that is the picture.

wrong.Pass; the low reached the 50-day: Look again: the 50-day runs well under this low. The line it tagged is the 20 EMA.
wrong.Pass; the line is falling: The 20 EMA is rising into the hold. A falling line would be off; this one is not.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the hold session. Which line did the low reach? Take it as a 20 EMA pullback or pass.
choices: Pass; the low reached the 50-day
Take it; the 20 EMA held
Take it; both lines were tagged
questions.why: Pass as a 20 EMA pullback. The hold low sat under the 50-day SMA, with the 20 EMA just above it. So the line the low reached was the 50-day. That is the 50-day form, judged on its own card. It stopped, best 0.56R.
questions.lesson_line: Name the line the low touched before you name the setup.

wrong.Take it; the 20 EMA held: The low went through the 20 EMA to the 50-day. The 20 EMA pullback's low holds above the 50-day.
wrong.Take it; both lines were tagged: Two lines tagged means the deeper one is the line. That is the 50-day card, not this one.

questions.q: A 20 EMA pullback stopped on day one for 1.3% to 2.5% is a loss the plan expected, not a broken rule.
questions.why: True. The failures in our data were all stopped on the first session with stops 1.3% to 2.5% wide; one ordinary red day took them. The stop is the exit, and the small loss is the cost of the tight stop.
questions.lesson_line: Tight stops get taken by noise sometimes. That is the price of the small loss.
